title: Generic Quantum Security Under Alternate Group Operations
summary: Complete reductions cover Even–Mansour and Encrypted-CBC-MAC, while generic quantum-CPA security for other transformed classically secure schemes remains to be proved or refuted.

formal_statement.body: Does replacing the group operation of a classically secure symmetric-key scheme from $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$ with a suitable operation from an alternate finite group generically provide security against quantum chosen-plaintext attacks? Complete security reductions for this transformation are available for the Even--Mansour cipher and Encrypted-CBC-MAC, while for other schemes vulnerable to attacks by the Simon algorithm, the available result is only that changing from $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$ to alternatives such as $\mathbb{Z}/2^n$ or $S_n$ thwarts those attacks. The unresolved task is to prove or refute generic quantum-CPA security for the transformed classically secure schemes beyond the two cases with complete reductions.

scope.domain: Quantum security of symmetric-key cryptographic schemes under alternate finite-group operations.
assumptions: The symmetric-key scheme is classically secure.
parameters: The original group $(Z/2)^n$ and an alternate finite group: the original and replacement group structures
Quantum chosen-plaintext attacks: the target attack model
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute generic quantum-CPA security for the transformed classically secure schemes beyond Even–Mansour and Encrypted-CBC-MAC.

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents generic quantum-CPA security after replacing the group operation as a conjecture. It reports complete reductions only for Even–Mansour and Encrypted-CBC-MAC, and only attack-thwarting observations for the other Simon-vulnerable schemes.
